issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` may match unrelated tokens like `1s` inside a URL or string
issues.detail: The cheap pre-filter is sound in spirit: skip the expensive valueParser when no time-like token is present. But `\dm?s` will also fire on substrings like `url(foo1s.png)` or `"abc1ms"`. False positives only cost a parse (correctness preserved), so this is a nit, not a bug. Worth a comment noting it's an over-approximation gate.

issues.description: Right shape: cheap filter before expensive parse — SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE
issues.detail: This is the correct data-first move. The walker was paying for valueParser on every decl when most decls have no time token. A regex test on the raw string is the obvious filter. Measure-driven, minimal, no new abstraction. Leave it alone — this is what these fixes should look like.

issues.description: Reordering `propertyName` after the early-return is a small composition win
issues.detail: Moving `vendor.unprefixed(decl.prop.toLowerCase())` below the guard avoids a lowercase + unprefix call on every skipped decl. Tiny, but it's the right instinct: do nothing until you know you must. No change requested.

review.summary: A textbook small-and-composable fix: a cheap regex gate short-circuits the expensive valueParser path when no time token is present in the decl value. Data dominates — the shape of the input (most decls have no `s`/`ms`) makes the algorithm obvious. The regex is a deliberate over-approximation, which is fine because the slow path still validates; correctness is preserved. Minor nit: the pattern can match digits-then-`s` inside URLs or strings, worth a one-line comment. Otherwise leave it alone.
